resolution: Fixed: covered-country names grounded in the fetched 10 U.S.C. 4872(f)(2) (registered as referencedSource usc-10-4872); names verified against that statute.
notes: Coverage/omission pass: all seven source provisions (short title; study of national security + cybersecurity risks; covered-device scope with three-prong supply nexus; 1-year report to named House/Senate committees; intra-Department consultation; covered-country cross-reference to 10 USC 4872(f)(2); Secretary definition) are represented in the analysis — no material omissions. DOMINANT MATERIAL DEFECT (4 rows, one root cause): the analysis enumerates 'China, Iran, North Korea, or Russia' as the covered countries in summary, brief, top_lines[0].subs[0], and changes.added[0]. Those countries appear NOWHERE in the fetched source; the bill defines 'covered country' solely by cross-reference to section 4872(f)(2) of title 10, U.S. Code, which was not fetched or registered as a referencedSource. Per the hostile source-only rule this is extrinsic/training-knowledge. Note the Section 2 detail item already states the faithful phrasing ('covered countries are those specified in section 4872(f)(2)...') — the top-level fields should mirror that instead of naming nations, or the 4872(f)(2) statute should be fetched + registered before naming any country. featured_quotes (CR quote) and versionChanges were out of scope for this bill-text-only audit and not verifiable against the bill source.
